newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** Most banks, government offices and companies closed for Moslem festival of Ramzan Id but Bombay and National bourses open for business
** Sikh-Hindu alliance in India's northern state of Punjab wins overwhelming majority in key local polls, officials say

They say the pro-Sikh Akali Dal Party wins 68 seats, and its rightwing Hindu nationalist ally, India's main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), takes 18 with 108 results declared in the 117-member state assembly
** India's budgetary deficit, as measured on January 24, 1997, already more than double the estimates for 1996/97 (April-March), central bank says
The central bank says it is concerned over a slowdown in industrial growth, high interest rates (both nominal and real) and a decline in growth of exports
** Japanese investors led by powerful car makers have plunged into India's alluring market but face daunting challenges ahead

"There is a need for elimination and relaxation of regulations so that we can enhance free competition," said Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of Toyota Motor Corp, part of a delegation representing Japan's influential business association Keidanren

** U.S. energy giant Enron Corp submits $10 billion proposal to Indian government to build power plants able to generate a total 10,000 megawatts of electricity, the Press Trust of India says on the weekend
** India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index rises to 7.66 percent in the week ending January 25 from 7.48 percent in the previous week
